results.name: Nat.ModEq
results.docstring: Modular equality. `n.ModEq a b`, or `a ≡ b [MOD n]`, means that `a % n = b % n`.

results.name: Nat.ModEq.dvd_iff
results.source_text:
theorem dvd_iff (h : a ≡ b [MOD m]) (hdm : d ∣ m) : d ∣ a ↔ d ∣ b := by
  simp only [← modEq_zero_iff_dvd]
  replace h := h.of_dvd hdm
  exact ⟨h.symm.trans, h.trans⟩

results.name: Nat.modEq_iff_dvd
results.source_text:
theorem modEq_iff_dvd : a ≡ b [MOD n] ↔ (n : ℤ) ∣ b - a := by
  rw [ModEq, eq_comm, ← Int.natCast_inj, Int.natCast_mod, Int.natCast_mod,
    Int.emod_eq_emod_iff_emod_sub_eq_zero, Int.dvd_iff_emod_eq_zero]

results.name: Nat.modEq_zero_iff_dvd
results.source_text: theorem modEq_zero_iff_dvd : a ≡ 0 [MOD n] ↔ n ∣ a := by rw [ModEq, zero_mod, dvd_iff_mod_eq_zero]

results.name: Nat.modEq_iff_dvd'
results.source_text:
/-- A variant of `modEq_iff_dvd` with `Nat` divisibility -/
theorem modEq_iff_dvd' (h : a ≤ b) : a ≡ b [MOD n] ↔ n ∣ b - a := by
  rw [modEq_iff_dvd, ← Int.natCast_dvd_natCast, Int.ofNat_sub h]

results.name: ZMod.val_neg_of_ne_zero
results.source_text:
theorem val_neg_of_ne_zero {n : ℕ} [nz : NeZero n] (a : ZMod n) [na : NeZero a] :
    (-a).val = n - a.val := by simp_all [neg_val a, na.out]

results.name: ZMod.val_ne_zero
results.source_text:
theorem val_ne_zero {n : ℕ} (a : ZMod n) : a.val ≠ 0 ↔ a ≠ 0 :=
  (val_eq_zero a).not

results.name: ZMod.val_neg'
results.source_text:
@[simp]
theorem val_neg' {n : ZMod 0} : (-n).val = n.val :=
  Int.natAbs_neg n

results.name: ZMod.neg_val'
results.source_text:
theorem neg_val' {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a : ZMod n) : (-a).val = (n - a.val) % n :=
  calc
    (-a).val = val (-a) % n := by rw [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (-a).val_lt]
    _ = (n - val a) % n :=
      Nat.ModEq.add_right_cancel' (val a)
        (by
          rw [Nat.ModEq, ← val_add, neg_add_cancel, tsub_add_cancel_of_le a.val_le, Nat.mod_self,
            val_zero])

results.name: ZMod.val
results.source_text:
/-- `val a` is a natural number defined as:
  - for `a : ZMod 0` it is the absolute value of `a`
  - for `a : ZMod n` with `0 < n` it is the least natural number in the equivalence class

See `ZMod.valMinAbs` for a variant that takes values in the integers.
-/
def val : ∀ {n : ℕ}, ZMod n → ℕ
  | 0 => Int.natAbs
  | n + 1 => ((↑) : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ)

results.name: ZMod.val_add
results.source_text:
theorem val_add {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a b : ZMod n) : (a + b).val = (a.val + b.val) % n := by
  cases n
  · cases NeZero.ne 0 rfl
  · apply Fin.val_add

results.name: ZMod.val_add_le
results.source_text:
theorem val_add_le {n : ℕ} (a b : ZMod n) : (a + b).val ≤ a.val + b.val := by
  cases n
  · simpa [ZMod.val] using! Int.natAbs_add_le _ _
  · simpa [ZMod.val_add] using! Nat.mod_le _ _

results.name: Physlib.PiTensorProduct.instAddCommMonoidElim_physlib
results.source_text:
/-- Given two maps `s1` and `s2` whose targets carry an instance of an additive commutative
  monoid, the target of the sum of these two maps also carry an instance thereof. -/
instance : (i : ι1 ⊕ ι2) → AddCommMonoid ((fun i => Sum.elim s1 s2 i) i) := fun i =>
  match i with
  | Sum.inl i => inst1 i
  | Sum.inr i => inst2 i
